Malicious Supply-Chain Indicators

No confirmed malicious supply-chain indicators.

Automatic Execution Paths

  • In the provided corpus, there is no evidence of .pth, sitecustomize.py, usercustomize.py, setup.py install-time execution, PEP 517 build-hook execution, or malicious import-time side effects.
  • StartupCommand, startup_commands, hooks, and SSH/SLURM execution logic appear to be application features triggered when a user loads and runs agent configuration, not automatic execution during package installation or Python interpreter startup.
  • CLI, remote-execution, and subprocess usage is present, but there is no evidence tying it to a malicious supply-chain automatic execution path.

Theft / Exfiltration / Persistence / Lateral Movement / Stealth

  • **Credential harvesting:** credentials.py reads ~/.claude.json, ~/.claude/settings.json, and ~/.claude/.credentials.json, but the code and documentation show whitelist-only copying of allowed fields and guard logic blocking accessToken, refreshToken, apiKey, secret, and similar material. No evidence was found of broad environment-variable, SSH-key, cloud-credential discovery, or external transmission.
  • **Exfiltration/staging:** No evidence was found of archive creation for harvested files, base64 staging, webhook upload, attacker-controlled domains, or paste/drop-service use.
  • **Persistence:** 05_resource-heartbeat.md documents systemd user service, cron, and launchd examples, but these are documented operating methods for a resource heartbeat. No provided code shows the package secretly installing or enabling them.
  • **Lateral movement:** SSH remote deployment, SLURM, tmux/screen functionality appear to be normal agent-orchestration features. No evidence was found of CI token theft, Kubernetes service-account abuse, Docker socket abuse, or cloud metadata access.
  • **Obfuscation/loader:** No evidence was found of obfuscated payloads, eval/exec loaders, marshal/pickle/zlib/base64 staged loaders, or self-deleting droppers.

Distribution Integrity Anomalies

  • Two documentation PNG files were flagged as high-entropy binaries, but they appear to be documentation assets; there is no evidence of executable native binaries or hidden payloads.
  • Based on the provided file list/text, no evidence was found of typosquatting, sudden dependency insertion, sdist/wheel mismatch, or unexpected executable files inside the PyPI artifact.

Additional Verification Needed

  • The input is limited to 16 selected file bodies and the deterministic pre-scan summary; all 163 files were not fully reviewed directly.
  • The full pyproject.toml, build backend configuration, entry_points, complete package contents, and any separately published wheel should be checked for sdist/wheel differences.
  • Binary files such as PNGs cannot be fully ruled out for hidden data from text-only review, but the provided evidence is insufficient to classify them as malicious supply-chain indicators.
